label: Arista 7280SR-48C6 (48x 1/10G SFP+, 6x 100G QSFP)
description: Arista 7280SR-48C6 - 1RU deep-buffer switch router (7280R series): 48x 1/10G SFP+ (Ethernet1-48) plus 6x 100G QSFP (Ethernet49-54) that also take 40G or break out to 25G/10G. 2.16 Tbps, 4 GB buffer, 2 hot-swap PSUs.
notes: Arista 7280R data sheet, 'Arista 7280SR-48C6' bullet: "7280SR-48C6: 48 port SFP+ and 6 ports 100GbE" / "Offers 48 wire speed 1/10G SFP+ ports" / "Six 100G QSFP ports allow choice of 6 x 100GbE, 24x 25GbE, 6x 40GbE, or 24x 10GbE" / "2.16Tbps of wire speed performance with 4GB of buffer". Hence SFP+ cages (10G maximum, so sfp+ and not sfp28) on Ethernet1-48 with 1/10G caps, and QSFP28 on Ethernet49-54 with the 10/25/40/100G envelope the breakout sentence lists. The sheet contradicts itself on the breakout count: its Model Comparison row prints "Max 25GbE Ports 12 / Max 10GbE Ports 24" while the bullet for the same six cages prints 24x 25GbE / 24x 10GbE, so the caps state the envelope and claim no breakout count. The same table flags this SKU End of Sale (E). This spec replaces devices/arista/7280sr.json, which modelled a device called "7280SR" - not a SKU anywhere in the sheet - as 8 x 100G with no sources. The real name and the AlgoMatch variant the sheet's feature row names beside it (7280SRA-48C6) are kept as aliases so old references still resolve.
